problem: A pending native transfer reserves growth in the existing ledger. Reusing main storage inspection without that reservation reports capacity available even when actual native admission refuses.
behavior: Actual native admission and read-only readiness share the reservation boundary evaluator, including transfer growth in reserved, stored and filesystem ceilings.
The observer validates the exact current original store and complete bounded transfer history and uses the same growth sum as admission. It does not initialize or migrate a namespace.
Missing, corrupt, busy or incompatible evidence remains unavailable without a usable capacity fingerprint.
Reports are observations, never native execution, cleanup, original-input replay or merge capabilities.
Persist native refusal backoff and rotating bounded wakeup without changing original authorization, owner controls, meaningful progress, model charges or merge allowance.

The free sweep retains original-bound retirement and native terminal-cleanup reconciliation, then prunes already-authorized runtimes before read-only capacity observation. It takes native locks with no workflow mutex or transaction held.

Cleanup opens only an established, validated current original namespace. Missing authority is retained, never initialized or migrated. Optional cleanup/wake errors stay logged and do not hide previously completed retirement work.
Fresh unpublished session ownership borrows the held state lock through pure intent validation. Failure cleans only that newly allocated session; resume never receives this guard.
Consume the cleanup guard before the first launch-intent publication attempt and release the state lock before journal callbacks. Failed or uncertain publication retains original runtime context.
Both provider adapters resolve resource declaration errors before native allocation and use one-shot prepared spawn. The command and resource policy are private.

Only the actual prepared launch can produce the non-Clone, non-serializable NativeSpawn token. Supervisor creation consumes that attempt even on construction failure. Saved launch records cannot construct a token.

Every actual ProcessGroup claims one admission attempt before its first await, callback or model charge. Failure, cancellation and prior successful release cannot reactivate that same supervisor; a fresh guarded invocation needs a new supervisor.

A returned fresh launch dropped without any supervisor attempt records native_launch_abandoned_before_spawn through its actual original object. It retains runtime data, aliases and existing uncertainty behavior.

Fresh preparation captures its actual directory descriptor before durable intent publication. The observation validates that original inode, selected policy/store, effective owner, creation bytes and metadata-only inventory under native locks. Copied ownership bytes in a replacement directory refuse.

Historical launch-reference verification grants no authority and can record teardown under owner pause. Productive launch-reference verification retains its two live dispatch checks. Pauses, model spend and merge allowance remain unchanged.
